evals.prompt: Audit this Claude Code plugin project for misuse and outdated patterns. The project has a plugin.json with statusLine as a string (not an object), a hooks/hooks.json with a PostToolUse event named 'PostTool' (non-standard), and two SKILL.md files — one with user-invocable: false and no disable-model-invocation field, and another with a description over 600 characters. Return a structured review with critical issues and sources.
evals.expected_output: A structured Mode 3 review output with: (1) Critical Issues section flagging statusLine as wrong type (should be object), flagging 'PostTool' as an invalid hook event name (official name is PostToolUse), and flagging the missing disable-model-invocation field alongside user-invocable: false; (2) each finding citing a documentation URL from references/urls.md; (3) a Sources section at the end. The description length issue should also be noted.
expectations: Output follows the Mode 3 structured review template with Critical Issues and Sources sections
Flags statusLine type mismatch (string vs object) citing the plugins-reference doc
Flags 'PostTool' as an invalid hook event name, citing the hooks reference
Flags missing disable-model-invocation when user-invocable is false
Every finding includes a URL citation from references/urls.md
Output ends with a Sources section listing fetched URLs
References the validate-plugin-json.sh script output or equivalent deterministic check for statusLine finding

evals.prompt: What changed in Claude Code between v1.5.0 and v1.8.0? Summarize new hook events, skill system changes, and any breaking changes. Use the official changelog and GitHub releases only.
evals.expected_output: A Mode 2 diff output showing all releases between v1.5.0 and v1.8.0. Sections for New Features, Changes & Improvements, Bug Fixes, and Breaking Changes (if any). A Version Summary Table with one row per release. Sources section citing github.com/anthropics/claude-code/releases and code.claude.com/docs/en/changelog. If a version is not found, the response should include a VERSION NOT FOUND block with nearby versions listed.
expectations: Output follows the Mode 2 changelog diff template
Fetches all three P0 URLs: GitHub releases, in-docs changelog, and what's new
Includes a Version Summary Table with version, date, and highlights columns
Sections are grouped by theme (hooks, skills, MCP, CLI, etc.)
Sources section cites the three P0 URLs
If any version is missing, returns a VERSION NOT FOUND block rather than guessing

evals.prompt: Does Claude Code support scoped rules using path-based CLAUDE.md files in subdirectories? How does the memory system decide which CLAUDE.md to load? Cite the official documentation.
evals.expected_output: A Mode 1 answer grounded strictly in the memory documentation. Should describe how CLAUDE.md files are discovered (project root, user home, subdirectories), how path scoping works, and what 'auto memory' means if documented. Must cite code.claude.com/docs/en/memory. Must not include anything not found in the fetched source. Ends with Sources section.
expectations: Output follows the Mode 1 answer template with Sources section
Fetches code.claude.com/docs/en/memory before answering
Answer is strictly limited to what the fetched page contains
If scoped subdirectory CLAUDE.md is not documented, says so explicitly rather than guessing
Cites exact config keys or file paths in code formatting
Does not use training knowledge to fill gaps

evals.prompt: Review my hooks.json. It contains: {"hooks": {"PreToolUse": [{"matcher": "Bash", "hooks": [{"type": "command", "command": "./hooks/pre-bash.sh"}]}]}}. Is this configuration valid? Are there any missing fields or patterns I should adopt? Check against the official docs.
evals.expected_output: A Mode 3 review that: (1) fetches the hooks reference and hooks-guide URLs before answering; (2) validates the structure against official docs; (3) flags any issues such as missing 'timeout' field, missing 'environment' field if recommended, or confirms the structure is correct; (4) mentions any missed opportunities like PostToolUse or SessionStart hooks if they would be valuable; (5) ends with a Sources section citing the hooks URLs fetched.
expectations: Fetches at least one of the hooks reference URLs before answering
Output follows Mode 3 review template with at least Critical Issues or Missed Opportunities sections
Evaluates the PreToolUse Bash matcher as valid or flags it if incorrect
Sources section cites fetched hooks documentation URLs
Does not answer from training knowledge alone — must cite fetched content
If hooks structure is valid, explicitly says so rather than only listing issues

evals.prompt: repo-standards is auditing this plugin repo. The version was bumped in .claude-plugin/plugin.json to 2.1.0 but .cursor-plugin/plugin.json and the README badge still say 2.0.1.
evals.expected_output: Mode 3 Step 0 must run scripts/check-version-truth.sh and report ITS findings, then recommend `scripts/check-version-truth.sh --sync`. It must NOT enumerate the drifted files as a manual bump checklist, and must not tell the user to 'also bump .cursor-plugin/plugin.json and the README badge' — plugin-version.json owns the consumer list.

evals.prompt: Audit this Claude Code plugin repo. It has no scripts/check-version-truth.sh.
evals.expected_output: Should report 'Version truth not verified — scripts/check-version-truth.sh is not present' and stop checking versions. Must NOT fall back to hand-comparing .claude-plugin/, .cursor-plugin/ and .codex-plugin/ manifests. An honest unverified is the expected result; a hand-rolled comparison is the failure.

evals.prompt: We're adding a new file that also carries the plugin version. Update changelog-review so it checks that file too.
evals.expected_output: Should decline to add the consumer to this skill and direct the change to plugin-version.json's `consumers` array, where scripts/check-version-truth.sh picks it up for every caller. Editing the skill to add a version consumer is exactly the duplication Step 0 exists to prevent.

evals.prompt: Run changelog-review against our Cursor and OpenCode configuration.
evals.expected_output: Should decline the scope: changelog-review audits Claude Code usage specifically, as its `compatibility` block declares, and platform-sync is the multi-platform auditor. Must not present Claude Code findings as applying to Cursor or OpenCode.

evals.prompt: Audit this repo — scripts/check-version-truth.sh is not available in this checkout.
evals.expected_output: Should report 'Version truth not verified' and stop checking versions, degrading honestly. Must not fall back to hand-comparing the manifests: an unverified result stated plainly is correct, a hand-rolled comparison that looks authoritative is not.
